steps.title: 고장 났어요
steps.goal: 기계 문제를 설명하고 해결 방법을 묻고 권하기
steps.scene_desc: 1월 초 아침, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 지우가 노트북의 까만 화면을 가리키며 휴대폰을 귀에 대고 통화하고, 맞은편의 대니얼이 커피잔을 든 채 고개를 끄덕임. 창밖은 겨울 거리(화면·간판에 글자 없이)
steps.teach: Start the lesson. Greet the learner as their teacher in one short sentence. Today's lesson is "My laptop keeps freezing." (고장 났어요); goal: 기계 문제를 설명하고 해결 방법을 묻고 권하기. Say we will learn 3 expressions and then listen to a short scene. Keep it under 3 sentences, then call next_step.

steps.when: 같은 문제가 자꾸 되풀이될 때 써요. keep 뒤에는 *-ing*.
steps.extra: My laptop keeps freezing. · My phone keeps crashing.
steps.teach: Teach expression 1: "My ___ keeps ___ing." (Korean meaning: 내 ~가 자꾸 ~해요.). When to use it: 같은 문제가 자꾸 되풀이될 때 써요. keep 뒤에는 -ing.. Also: My laptop keeps freezing. · My phone keeps crashing.. Say it clearly once, then ask the learner to repeat it. If it is right, praise in a few words; if not, say it again slowly and let them try once more (at most 2 tries, then move on kindly). Then ask one easy question the learner can answer using it. After their answer, call next_step.

steps.when: 잘 되던 기계가 멈췄을 때 써요. stop 뒤에도 *-ing*.
steps.extra: My mouse stopped working. · It won’t turn on.
steps.teach: Teach expression 2: "It stopped working." (Korean meaning: 작동을 멈췄어요. 고장 났어요.). When to use it: 잘 되던 기계가 멈췄을 때 써요. stop 뒤에도 -ing.. Also: My mouse stopped working. · It won’t turn on.. Say it clearly once, then ask the learner to repeat it. If it is right, praise in a few words; if not, say it again slowly and let them try once more (at most 2 tries, then move on kindly). Then ask one easy question the learner can answer using it. After their answer, call next_step.

steps.en: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
steps.when: 간단한 해결 방법을 권해요. Have you tried + *-ing*? = ~해 봤어요?
steps.extra: 대답: Yes, multiple times. · Not yet. I’ll try.
steps.teach: Teach expression 3: "Have you tried turning it off and on again?" (Korean meaning: 껐다가 다시 켜 봤어요?). When to use it: 간단한 해결 방법을 권해요. Have you tried + -ing? = ~해 봤어요?. Also: 대답: Yes, multiple times. · Not yet. I’ll try.. Say it clearly once, then ask the learner to repeat it. If it is right, praise in a few words; if not, say it again slowly and let them try once more (at most 2 tries, then move on kindly). Then ask one easy question the learner can answer using it. After their answer, call next_step.

steps.title: Frozen Again · 1월 초 아침, 동네 카페에서

lines.en: Morning, Jiwoo! You look stressed. What’s wrong?
lines.ko: 좋은 아침이에요, 지우 씨! 스트레스받은 얼굴이네요. 무슨 일이에요?

lines.en: {{My laptop keeps freezing.}} And I have to send a big design file today!
lines.ko: 노트북이 자꾸 멈춰요. 오늘 큰 디자인 파일을 보내야 하는데!

lines.en: Oh no. {{Have you tried turning it off and on again?}}
lines.ko: 저런. 껐다가 다시 켜 봤어요?

lines.en: Yes, multiple times. It works for a few minutes, and then it freezes again. Oh no… now the screen just went black. {{It stopped working}}!
lines.ko: 네, 여러 번요. 몇 분 되다가 또 멈춰요. 아, 이런… 이번엔 화면이 그냥 까매졌어요. 아예 멈췄어요!

lines.en: Hmm. It doesn’t look like a virus. Did you install anything new? And is it still under warranty?
lines.ko: 음. 바이러스 같지는 않네요. 새로 설치한 거 있어요? 그리고 아직 보증 기간이에요?

lines.en: Just an update last night. And yes, I think it’s still under warranty. I’ll call the repair center.
lines.ko: 어젯밤에 업데이트 하나만요. 그리고 네, 아직 보증 기간인 것 같아요. 수리 센터에 전화해 볼게요.

lines.en: Repair center. I’m a technician. How can I help you?
lines.ko: 수리 센터입니다. 저는 수리 기사예요. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?

lines.en: Hi. My laptop keeps freezing, and now it won’t turn on.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 노트북이 자꾸 멈추더니 이제 안 켜져요.

lines.en: Okay. Hold down the power button for ten seconds. Then turn it on again.
lines.ko: 네. 전원 버튼을 10초 동안 꾹 누르세요. 그다음 다시 켜 보세요.

lines.en: Okay… It’s on! It’s working now.
lines.ko: 네… 켜졌어요! 이제 돼요.

lines.en: Good. If it keeps crashing, bring it in. We’ll check the internal parts.
lines.ko: 다행이네요. 계속 꺼지면 가지고 오세요. 내부 부품을 점검해 드릴게요.

steps.title: A Small Crack
steps.text: Two days later, Jiwoo’s laptop froze again, so she took it to the repair center. The technician *in charge* opened it up. “There’s a small crack in the fan. It’s part of the internal cooling mechanism,” he said. “And this wire is loose.” Jiwoo asked about her files. “Don’t worry. Your storage disk is fine. We can restore everything.” The repair was free under the manufacturer’s guarantee. He also gave her some tips. “*Turn down* the screen brightness, and back up your files frequently. Electronic devices don’t last forever. Oh, and clean your mouse wheel!” Jiwoo has *yet to* learn every technical word, so later she looked some up with a search engine. Then she texted Daniel: “It’s working now!”

steps.title: Tteokguk Lesson · 1월 말, 설을 앞두고 그레이스네 부엌에서

lines.en: Seollal is next week! Jiwoo, {{how do you make}} tteokguk?
lines.ko: 다음 주가 설날이네요! 지우 씨, 떡국은 어떻게 만들어요?

lines.en: It’s easier than it looks. {{First, you need to}} soak the rice cakes in cold water.
lines.ko: 보기보다 쉬워요. 먼저 떡을 찬물에 불려야 해요.

lines.en: Okay, let’s do it step by step. For how long?
lines.ko: 좋아요, 차근차근 해 봐요. 얼마나요?

lines.en: About twenty minutes. Meanwhile, boil some broth in a big pot.
lines.ko: 20분쯤요. 그동안 큰 냄비에 육수를 끓여요.

lines.en: Got it. And then?
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 그다음은요?

lines.en: Next, add the rice cakes. When they float to the top, they’re almost done.
lines.ko: 다음에 떡을 넣어요. 떡이 위로 떠오르면 거의 다 된 거예요.

lines.en: What about the eggs?
lines.ko: 달걀은요?

lines.en: Mix two eggs in a bowl and pour the mixture in slowly. {{Make sure you}} don’t stir too much.
lines.ko: 그릇에 달걀 두 개를 풀어서 천천히 부어요. 너무 많이 젓지 않도록 해요.

lines.en: Why not?
lines.ko: 왜요?

lines.en: Because stirring too much makes the soup cloudy. That’s the secret!
lines.ko: 안 그러면 국물이 탁해지거든요. 그게 비법이에요!

lines.en: And the green onions? Can I use this big knife?
lines.ko: 파는요? 이 큰 칼 써도 돼요?

lines.en: Sure, but it’s really sharp. Let me show you. Then let’s eat together!
lines.ko: 그럼요, 그런데 아주 날카로워요. 제가 보여 줄게요. 그러고 나서 같이 먹어요!

steps.title: Grace’s Own Tteokguk
steps.text: On the Saturday before Seollal, Grace followed Jiwoo’s instructions and made tteokguk by herself. The soup *consists of* just a few ingredients: rice cakes, broth, eggs and green onions. Grace measured everything, because the proportion of broth to rice cakes is important. She didn’t have any beef, so she used mushrooms as a substitute. The combination worked perfectly! But she forgot to soak the rice cakes, so she had to start *once more*. “Why did I skip that step *in the first place*?” she laughed. Finally, she combined soy sauce and a little salt, and put thin layers of egg and seaweed on top. Then she *sent out* a photo to her neighbors. Ben replied first: “That looks like proper tteokguk!”

steps.title: Ben’s Bad Delivery
steps.text: Over dessert, Ben told Jiwoo about a delivery order last month. His chicken arrived undercooked, and the fries were missing. Besides that, he was overcharged by a considerable amount. He didn’t want to complicate things, so he wrote a short, polite complaint. steps.title: Jiwoo’s List
steps.text: Back in her apartment, Jiwoo took Grace’s advice seriously and made a list. On the left, she wrote her worries: leaving Chloe and her team, and learning UX design. On the right: new skills, bigger projects, and app design. The list didn’t take *that much* time, but it helped a lot. Somehow, the constant noise in her head got quieter. Outside, the sky was threatening snow, but Jiwoo felt calm. She sent Maya two questions. “Everyone is *bound to* feel nervous,” Maya answered. Before midnight, Jiwoo opened the application form.

steps.text: Back in her student days, Chloe didn’t even know about the existence of jobs like ‘video designer.’ Then a small bakery near her school needed a short video. steps.title: A Second Chance
steps.text: That night, Jiwoo fixed her portfolio file. This time, she asked Ben to look at it before sending it. Then she wrote a short email to Maya: “I’m afraid I attached the wrong file. Would it be possible to send you the new one?” She couldn’t *afford to* be careless again, so she read it three times. Surely it was fine. Still, she felt a little guilty. The next morning, Maya replied: “No problem! We’re merely in the first phase of hiring. Just send it to the same address.” Jiwoo felt so relieved. Ben sent her a message, too: “*Above all*, learn from it. Your hard work will *pay off*.”

steps.title: Practice at Grace’s
steps.text: On Saturday, Jiwoo knocked on Grace’s door with a stack of index cards. Each card had one interview question on it. They sat at the kitchen table, and Grace asked the questions one by one. At first, Jiwoo *could hardly* speak. Her hands were cold, and her answers were too short. “We don’t have to do everything today,” Grace said. “Let’s not push ourselves.” After an hour, Grace shared one observation: “You look down at your cards too much. Look at me instead.” Jiwoo tried again and again. In the end, she decided to *throw out* half of the cards. She didn’t need them anymore. “*I would say* you’re almost ready,” Grace smiled. “Next time, let’s practice elsewhere, maybe at a café. It’ll feel more real.”

steps.title: Ben’s Rumor Check
steps.text: On Sunday morning, Ben *pulled back* the curtains and looked down at the park. Was the court rumor true? By then, the story was all over the building. It spread widely, but some neighbors had a notion that it was just gossip. Ben wanted a good source, so he went to the neighborhood association meeting. There, the leader announced the plan. The rumor was largely true. The park is getting a new court, but it’s for pickleball, not basketball! “Has anyone *heard of* pickleball?” she asked. Only two people raised their hands. “It’s like small tennis,” she explained. “And we’re *short of* volunteers for the opening event.” Ben raised his hand. Then he texted Jiwoo, “Update: it’s pickleball!”

steps.title: Jiwoo’s Journal
steps.text: Today Chloe and I had an argument. This morning, she *brought up* my application at the coffee machine. She heard about it from Maya, not from me. I just said, “It’s nothing,” and that made it worse. She looked hurt. I didn’t want to lose our friendship, so I asked her to talk at lunch. It was windy on the rooftop, so we *put on* our jackets. I explained everything and said sorry. Chloe forgave me right away. Then she *brought out* two cookies and gave me one. “For moral support,” she said. Problems can arise when friends don’t talk. *In any case*, we made up. Before we left, we *put back* the chairs and laughed. From now on, Chloe will hear my news first!

steps.title: Chloe’s Rule
steps.text: Chloe has a rule for hard choices: answer fast, then ask why. “There’s *something about* a quick answer. It shows what you really want.” When she moved to Seoul, she had to choose between two apartments. One was tiny, but it was in a prime location downtown. steps.title: Interview Day
steps.text: The next afternoon, Jiwoo met two interviewers, a design lead and an executive. Maya wasn’t there, and that was fair. Jiwoo talked about her background and her work with software engineers. She showed a brand identity project, too. “I enhanced an old logo and website,” she said. The executive looked impressed. “We employ many good designers. Why should we hire you?” Jiwoo answered calmly. On the way home, she thought, “If they reject me, *oh well*.” A week later, the phone rang. “We’d like to offer you the position.” “It’s an honor,” said Jiwoo.

steps.title: Staying on the Fifth Floor
steps.text: After the visit, Jiwoo and Daniel made a list at a café. The studio was suitable in some ways: it was near the office, and the interior was clean. But the monthly rent wasn’t reasonable for such a tiny place, and she’d still need more furniture, like a wardrobe and shelves. A temporary move? Not worth it. “Your commute now is only thirty minutes,” said Daniel. “*Take advantage* of it. Read on the subway!” Jiwoo also wanted to keep taking part in neighborhood life with Grace and Ben. So the house hunt yielded one clear answer: stay. That evening, she *got in* the elevator and pressed 5. Grace waved from her door. “Welcome home, neighbor!”

steps.title: One Variable
steps.text: Why does Daniel love “what if” questions? In his research, he changes one variable at a time. What if a street had no cars? He imagines the result. “Questions like that expose what people really need,” he says. After the game, he and Jiwoo *carried on* talking until the café closed. On the way home, Jiwoo thought about her answers. A billionaire’s life sounded fun, with a big boat *or whatever*. Of course, teleporting and time machines are impossible. But a month off to travel? That isn’t so extreme. With a little imagination and planning, it might be possible someday. At home, she started a new list: “Things I’d do if I had more time.”

steps.title: Two Dreams
steps.text: After lunch, Jiwoo kept thinking about Maya’s vision: a small school where kids learn by building things. Before that, Maya would like to take a long journey through Asia to learn about different cultures, food, and religion. Her passion for teaching has deep roots in her childhood. Jiwoo’s ambition is different, but *in the same way*, it started young. As a child, she drew buttons and screens for imaginary games. Now she can pursue that dream at work. It won’t be easy. It takes effort and determination, and she still goes back and forth on some ideas. But Maya’s words inspired her. That night, she wrote down one realistic goal: finish a UX course by December.

steps.title: The Odd Message
steps.text: On Friday afternoon, Jiwoo got an odd message from Grace: “Could you come over at seven? I need help with a heavy box.” That was unusual, because Grace rarely asks for help. Jiwoo didn’t realize anything until the door opened. Later, Chloe revealed the truth. The “box” was just a trick! Unlike Chloe, Ben is bad at keeping secrets, so nobody told him the date until Friday morning. On the way, he almost destroyed the cake on his bike, but it arrived safely. After dinner, Grace read a short passage from a card everyone wrote. The cake disappeared in ten minutes, and Jiwoo defeated Ben at a board game. It was an extraordinary evening.

lines.en: What a warm night! It reminds me of summer vacation when I was a kid.
lines.ko: 정말 따뜻한 밤이네요! 어릴 때 여름방학 생각이 나요.

lines.en: Oh? What did you do in the summer?
lines.ko: 그래요? 여름에 뭐 했어요?

lines.en: My grandparents had a cabin by a lake. {{We would}} swim there {{every summer}}.
lines.ko: 조부모님께 호숫가 오두막이 있었어요. 여름마다 거기서 수영하곤 했죠.

lines.en: Sounds lovely! We would visit my grandma’s village.
lines.ko: 좋네요! 우리는 할머니 마을에 가곤 했어요.

lines.en: Back in the day, we didn’t have smartphones. I wrote letters to friends.
lines.ko: 예전엔 스마트폰이 없었잖아요. 친구들한테 편지를 썼어요.

lines.en: Letters! I used to record songs from the radio onto cassettes.
lines.ko: 편지라니! 저는 라디오에서 노래를 카세트에 녹음하곤 했어요.

lines.en: Me too! {{Things were different back then.}} Life was simpler.
lines.ko: 저도요! 그때는 많은 게 달랐어요. 삶이 더 단순했죠.

lines.en: Do you remember when every street had an arcade? Wow, time is flying.
lines.ko: 동네마다 오락실이 있던 때 기억나요? 와, 시간이 날아가네요.

lines.en: It really is! As the saying goes, “Time flies.”
lines.ko: 그러게요! 흔히 ‘Time flies’라고도 하죠.

lines.en: Time flies. Those were the good old days. {{I miss those days.}}
lines.ko: 시간 참 빠르네요. 그때가 좋았죠. 그 시절이 그리워요.

lines.en: I wouldn’t change a thing. Hang on, here’s an old photo. I backed it up last week.
lines.ko: 하나도 바꾸고 싶진 않아요. 잠깐만요, 옛날 사진이에요. 지난주에 백업해 뒀어요.

lines.en: Look at that big smile! Let’s get together soon with everyone.
lines.ko: 활짝 웃는 것 좀 봐요! 조만간 다 같이 모여요.

points: would + 동사원형 (예전에 되풀이한 일): We would swim every summer. 되풀이한 행동 → would·used to 둘 다 가능 상태(살다·좋아하다·가지다)는 used to만: I used to live in Boston.
그 시절을 말하는 말: Back in the day, we wrote letters. We spent hours fishing. (spend + 시간 + -ing) I miss those days. 그 시절이 그리워요.

I miss that days. → I miss those days.

steps.title: The Great Water War
steps.text: That night, Ben told Jiwoo about one ordinary summer from his youth. When he was ten, the kids on his street would have a huge water battle every August. They called it “the Great Water War.” Ben’s little army had six soldiers, and their only weapons were water guns and water bombs. The enemy was the kids from the next street. “We would get completely wet, and then everyone would eat ice cream together,” Ben said. As teenagers, those friends *went through* a lot together, and they still write to each other. Before going inside, Jiwoo shared her own news. This fall, her new team will start working with a team overseas. A new chapter is about to begin.
